name: Tobie Morgan Hitchcock

education.school: University College London (UCL School of Management)
education.notes: Graduated 2010 from UCL SoM's BSc IMB programme.
Thesis focused on versioning within distributed databases — directly seeded SurrealDB's multi-model design.

careerSteps.role: Undergraduate (BSc IMB) then MSc Software Engineering
careerSteps.company: UCL School of Management → University of Oxford
keyDecisions: Picked a business-flavoured information-management BSc at UCL rather than pure CS — gave commercial framing on top of technical content.
Followed with an Oxford MSc in Software Engineering, with a thesis on versioning in distributed databases — the seed of SurrealDB.
lessons: A business-info degree plus a CS masters can be a credible founder path — the masters thesis is where the founding idea can crystallise.
Picking a thesis topic that doubles as future product spec is high-leverage.
careerSteps.notes: Oxford MSc Software Engineering is part-time/modular (typical 2-4 years), often done alongside industry work — exact start/end years not public; the thesis on versioning in distributed databases was the conceptual seed of SurrealDB.

careerSteps.company: Pre-SurrealDB venture (with brother Jaime Morgan Hitchcock)
keyDecisions: Built a golf-course analytics platform with brother Jaime as technical co-founder.
Used a polyglot persistence stack — InfluxDB (time-series), OrientDB (graph), DynamoDB (KV/doc) and MySQL (relational) — all in one product.
Lived the operational pain of stitching together four databases; that pain became SurrealDB's wedge.
lessons: Build-something-small-first is undervalued: a niche SaaS (golf analytics) gave the founders enough real production scar tissue to see the multi-model database opportunity.
Build the tool you needed yourself — SurrealDB is literally the product the founders wished existed during this period.
Brother-as-co-founder pattern: deep, durable trust accelerates risk-taking but constrains team-scaling later.
careerSteps.notes: Pre-venture era of the duo's career; bootstrapped/under-the-radar. Mobile-cloud era infrastructure choices directly shaped the product hypothesis for the next chapter.

keyDecisions: Founded SurrealDB in 2021; open-sourced in August 2022 with a launch on Hacker News that hit #1 — Rust-based multi-model database (document, graph, time-series, relational in one engine).
Raised ~$6M seed in Nov 2022 led by FirstMark Capital; follow-on rounds taking total funding to ~$26M+ from FirstMark, Georgian, Crew Capital and others.
Positioned heavily around the AI-data infrastructure narrative — single store for vector + relational + graph queries.
Built in Rust to bet on performance and the dev-tools cohort that respects systems-language choices.
lessons: Open-source dev-tools require a credible technical artefact before fundraising — SurrealDB launched on Hacker News with working code first, then raised.
Single-engine multi-model is a contrarian bet against the polyglot-persistence orthodoxy; the wedge is the operational pain the founders personally felt.
European (London) infra startups can raise from top US infra investors (FirstMark) when the technical narrative is strong — geography is not the blocker it once was.
Pick the language for the cohort you want to recruit — Rust signals seriousness to systems engineers.
careerSteps.notes: AI-revolution era; database market is being reshuffled by vector/AI workloads. SurrealDB's bet is that the multi-model + AI-data convergence makes it a category-defining play. Still early; no exit, valuation undisclosed publicly.

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-founder & CEO of SurrealDB, London-based Rust multi-model database company; well-funded venture-backed startup positioning for the AI-data infrastructure wave. Pre-exit; paper wealth tied to private equity.

lessons.lesson: Build the tool you needed yourself — SurrealDB came directly from the pain of stitching together four databases for an earlier product.
Open-source first, fundraise second. A working artefact with GitHub stars is the strongest fundraising signal for dev-tools.
A masters thesis on a niche technical problem can directly become a fundable startup if the problem is recurring at industry scale.
lessons.source: inferred from Oxford MSc → SurrealDB link

lessons.lesson: European infra founders should pursue US infra VCs (FirstMark, Crew, Georgian) — they price differently and are comfortable with global teams.
